render_gates.description: A translucent garment layer is immediately readable rather than a vague bright or glossy region.
Weave, seam, stitched boundary, edge, or fold proves that the transmitting surface is textile.

Light and the requested underlying body, lower garment or background are partly transmitted through the same visible garment textile in a coherent direction. The transmitting layer and underlying owner must remain distinct; an unrequested opaque covering cannot replace the intended lower surface.
Overlaps, folds, stretch, and lighting change transparency consistently across the same material.
Glass, wetness, overexposure, invisible clothing, or transparent-body artifacts do not carry the requested textile effect.
